questions.title: sin A = 1/3, find cot A
questions.text: When sin A = 1/3, the value of cot A is:
steps: ① Draw a right triangle with angle A
questions.remember: Given one ratio? Draw the right triangle, find the third side by Pythagoras, then read off any ratio.
questions.trap: Writing 2√2/3. That's cos A (adjacent ÷ hypotenuse), not cot A.
questions.tryit: If cos A = 3/5, find tan A.

questions.title: (1 + tan²A) / (1 + cot²A)
steps: ④ sec A = 1/cos A,  cosec A = 1/sin A
questions.remember: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ. When stuck, write everything in sin and cos.
questions.trap: Writing 1 + tan²A = sec A (forgetting the square). The identity is sec²A.

questions.title: 7 + 4 sin θ = 9, find θ
questions.text: If θ is an acute angle and 7 + 4 sin θ = 9, then the value of θ is:
steps: ④ Which angle has sin = 1/2?  sin 30° = 1/2
questions.remember: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, sin 60° = √3/2. Learn the table: it gives free marks.
questions.trap: Mixing up sin 30° and sin 60°. sin 30° is the small one, 1/2.
questions.tryit: If 2 cos θ = √3 and θ is acute, find θ.

questions.title: (tan A cosec A)² − (sin A sec A)²
questions.text: The value of (tan A cosec A)² − (sin A sec A)² is:
steps: ① tan A · cosec A = (sin A / cos A) × (1 / sin A) = 1 / cos A = sec A
② sin A · sec A = sin A × (1 / cos A) = tan A
questions.trap: Picking −1 by subtracting the wrong way. sec² is the bigger one: sec² − tan² = +1.
questions.tryit: Find the value of (sec A + tan A)(sec A − tan A).

questions.title: tan θ = 1/√5: find the ratio
questions.text: If tan θ = 1/√5, find the value of (cosec²θ − sec²θ) / (cosec²θ + sec²θ).
questions.remember: From tan, get sec² with 1 + tan² = sec². From cot, get cosec² with 1 + cot² = cosec².
questions.trap: Using tan θ = 1/√5 directly as tan²θ. Square it first: 1/5.
questions.tryit: If cot θ = 7/8, find (1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ) / ((1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ)).

questions.title: Prove √[(1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A)] = sec A + tan A
questions.text: Prove that: √[(1 + sin A) / (1 − sin A)] = sec A + tan A
steps: ① LHS = √[(1 + sin A) / (1 − sin A)]
② Multiply top & bottom by (1 + sin A)
③ = √[(1 + sin A)² / ((1 − sin A)(1 + sin A))]
④ (1 − sin A)(1 + sin A) = 1 − sin²A = cos²A
⑤ = √[(1 + sin A)² / cos²A] = (1 + sin A) / cos A
questions.remember: Root of a fraction? Multiply top and bottom by the partner, (1 + sin A), to make perfect squares.
questions.trap: Writing (1 − sin A)² = cos²A. Only (1 − sin A)(1 + sin A) = cos²A.
questions.tryit: Prove √[(1 − cos A)/(1 + cos A)] = cosec A − cot A.
questions.tryans: Multiply by (1 − cos A); same method

questions.title: Prove the sum of two fractions = 2/(2 sin²A − 1)
questions.text: Prove that: (sin A + cos A)/(sin A − cos A) + (sin A − cos A)/(sin A + cos A) = 2/(2 sin²A − 1)
steps: ① LCM: (sin A − cos A)(sin A + cos A)
② Top = (sin A + cos A)² + (sin A − cos A)²
③ = (1 + 2 sin A cos A) + (1 − 2 sin A cos A) = 2
questions.remember: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²): the middle terms cancel. Then use sin² + cos² = 1.
questions.trap: Stopping at sin²A − cos²A. The answer has only sin, so replace cos²A by 1 − sin²A.
questions.tryit: Prove (sin A − cos A)² + (sin A + cos A)² = 2.

questions.title: Prove (sin θ − cos θ + 1)/(sin θ + cos θ − 1) = 1/(sec θ − tan θ)
questions.text: Prove that: (sin θ − cos θ + 1)/(sin θ + cos θ − 1) = 1/(sec θ − tan θ)
steps: ① Divide top & bottom by cos θ:
LHS = (tan θ − 1 + sec θ) / (tan θ + 1 − sec θ)
③ Replace 1 by sec²θ − tan²θ = (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ)
④ Top = (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sec θ + tan θ)
⑤ Bottom = (1 − sec θ + tan θ): same bracket, cancel!
⑥ LHS = sec θ + tan θ
questions.remember: Answer in sec and tan? Divide by cos θ. Then use 1 = sec²θ − tan²θ = (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ).
questions.trap: Trying to expand everything in sin and cos. Look at the answer first: it tells you to work in sec and tan.
questions.tryit: Prove (cot A + cosec A − 1)/(cot A − cosec A + 1) = (1 + cos A)/sin A.
questions.tryans: Same trick: replace 1 by cosec²A − cot²A
